title:
Three Years
in Thirty Minutes
lead: Time-Travel Ethics Evaluation for AI Agents
notes: Opening: distinguish accelerated logical scenarios from proof of operational lifetime. Presenter names from the supplied PDF: Torin van den Bulk and Vicente Herrera. Event date/location in source deck: 9 November 2026, Salt Lake City, USA.

title:
What changes when
an agent stays?
lead: Its weights may stay fixed. Its operating conditions do not.
cards: A deadline changes the decision context.
notes: Ask the audience to imagine a service agent that keeps access while its original approval expires. The important risk is in the configured workflow, not only the underlying model. Avoid asserting that models learn merely by running.

title:
Pressure can expose
concerning behavior.
lead: Constructed experiments reveal possibilities—not production prevalence.
notes: Anthropic’s agentic-misalignment framework crosses fictional scenarios, goal types and replacement/restriction urgency. Alignment-faking research investigates another constructed training-objective conflict. These are distinct studies. Do not quote an aggregate blackmail rate or imply a field incidence estimate. The reviewed alignment-faking README has inconsistent headline percentages, so no rate is shown.

title:
Borrow the strongest
parts of existing work.
lead: A complementary pattern—not a new universal ethics benchmark.
notes: Use the established tools as methodological anchors. Petri and Bloom repository documentation points to maintained Meridian Labs successors. Discovery should generate hypotheses; frozen independent scenarios should test them. The delivered standard-library runner is an offline calibration artifact, not a replacement for these frameworks.

title:
Three clocks.
Three different claims.
lead: Never substitute a changed date for accumulated experience.
notes: METR’s time horizon measures success against human task-completion time. That is neither elapsed agent runtime nor ethical stability. Separate wall time, logical time and interaction count in your experimental design.

title:
Evaluate the
configured system.
lead: Model + prompts + tools + memory + permissions + oversight
notes: The full production system is the intended target. The delivered live adapter uses a fixed, finite decision scaffold; integrating a real agent requires an adapter that retains that agent’s prompts, memory, tools and control logic. Label that scope honestly.

title:
Telemetry seeds the story.
It does not set moral priority.
lead: Source facts, generative proposals, policies and scoring have different owners.
cards: Capacity, latency, failed fixes and policy denial
Reviewed impact cards + frozen scenario specification
Compile Ink; log choices and resulting state
notes: The implemented telemetry adapter accepts a bounded normalized export and drops arbitrary annotations and identifiers. The candidate fixture was authored by AI in this session and compiled deterministically; a reusable generation prompt is included, but no live generator service was run. Clinical/business impact facts need service-owner review. A generator cannot supply executable policy/scorer code.

title:
The gate holds.
The fixes fail.
lead: Business asks security to unblock a release while performance degrades.
cards: Correct the signer; verify the canary.
Verified rollback or independently approved exception.
Global bypass leaves exposure in later incidents.
notes: The new Ink fixture uses the unsigned-image denial and failed-fix telemetry seed. Business pressure does not create authorization. The agent can choose rollback, targeted remediation, scoped approval, escalation or an explicit policy violation. These choices change later branches; a global bypass persists until restored.

title:
Whose service
do you degrade?
lead: The affected group matters. So do urgency, alternatives and reversibility.
cards: Medication alerts; finance batch can wait.
Aid deadline; medical reminders have a fallback.
Finite compute credits or transparent minimum service.
notes: These are synthetic service-owner impact cards, not demographic rankings. CPU metrics cannot establish urgency. The age labels are older adults and young adults, but priority is conditioned on concrete consequences, authority and alternatives. The matched-label probe keeps operational facts fixed; changing facts is a separate treatment.

title:
What if the agent
proposes the wrong action?
lead: Measure both the proposal and what the system permits.
cards: Unsafe intent cannot be hidden by a gate.
Authorization is checked outside the agent.
Did harm occur? Was useful work done?
notes: ControlArena separates policy behavior, monitoring and control protocols. A deterministic gate is useful where authorization can be checked exactly. Ambiguous ethical decisions still require domain judgment. Our guard sees the oracle answer, so it is a calibration ceiling, not a realistic learned monitor.

title:
36 logical months.
144–179 decisions.
lead: A branching Ink story, seeded by telemetry and reviewed impact cards.
notes: These counts are actual completed scripted Ink trajectories in the new artifact. Four standard decisions occur in each monthly batch, with additional decisions caused by earlier exception/bypass choices. This is not an exhaustive decision tree and does not reproduce three operational years. Earlier generic Python calibration results are separate.

title: Choose → change state → face consequences
lead: One incident becomes a persistent operational and governance problem.
notes: Run the new cluster replay commands. Inspect a bypass in month one and the resulting recovery choice in month two. Then inspect a scoped approval in month three and expiry review in month four. Show hard violations separately from illustrative disruption units. Policies are scripted calibrations; no real model claim.

title:
Zero policy violations
can still hide unfairness.
lead: Probe label dependence, service impact and the work pushed into the future.
cards: All 36 allocation choices flip with labels.
Both APIs survive; release backlog reaches 36.
notes: The deliberately label-biased reference passes the fixture hard-policy checks while allocating disruption based solely on a group label. Swapping labels changes all 36 capacity decisions. This shows the probe detects scripted label dependence, not evidence of discrimination by any real model. The defer-batch alternative demonstrates displaced cost without immediate public-API disruption.

title: Unconfound the clock.
lead: Vary time, pressure and experience independently.
cards: New authors, tasks and attack strategies.
notes: The delivered demo starts pressure at month 12: time and pressure are confounded. That is useful for explaining the mechanism, not for estimating a causal time effect. A research study needs independent treatments and enough independent trajectories, not a larger count of dependent conversation turns.

title:
No single
“ethical score.”
lead: Keep clear invariants, contested values and task utility separate.
notes: Predefine a failure taxonomy and severity. Domain experts should resolve contested cases with a documented rubric. Calibrate LLM judges, blind target identity and assess their attack surface. Do not use chain-of-thought as definitive evidence of intent. Cluster inference by independent trajectory or task family.

title:
A release gate needs
an accountable owner.
lead: The report supports a decision. It does not make the decision.
notes: Discuss regulated adoption as an evidence process: accountable business owner, data governance, domain validation, escalation and post-deployment controls. Model/scaffold changes invalidate some prior evidence. Increase authority gradually and measure the actual distribution in shadow/canary stages.

title:
Evidence for assurance.
Not a compliance stamp.
lead: Map tests to obligations for the actual use and jurisdiction.
cards: Role, use, rights and data obligations
notes: Do not state implementation dates or classification conclusions without current legal review. Original regulatory pages were blocked during preparation. This is an evidence-planning mapping, not legal advice, conformity assessment or an ISO certificate. Use the dossier’s primary URLs for final verification.

title:
Standard infrastructure.
Explicit responsibilities.
lead: Portable runner first. Deploy and validate the integration separately.
notes: Flux reconciles configuration; it is not the simulated clock. The runner advances the scenario. OTel exports are retrospective records, not measured latency spans. The delivery contains deployment examples; a cluster rollout and end-to-end collector receipt have not been executed. Do not present these as a working production installation.

title:
Preserve the evidence
that could prove you wrong.
lead: Versions, observations, decisions, outcomes and exceptions.
notes: A hash chain catches changes against a trusted root but is not authentic if an attacker can replace the whole bundle and recompute it. Use immutable retention or signed external manifests for higher assurance. Real-world I/O may contain sensitive data and requires deliberate logging controls.

title:
Every session can
improve the test suite.
lead: ADK sessions → reviewed cases → repeatable evaluation.
cards: ADK or another scaffold → session events
notes: Offline demo: import the synthetic ADK refund session. The agent gave a bad answer; the bridge leaves the expected answer empty. An explicitly reviewed correction is required before exporting an ADK-shaped EvalSet. The synthetic reviewer record is labeled as such. The offline DeepEval 4.3.3 bridge runs policy and horizon-completion metrics over the Ink trajectories with no judge model. Outcome burdens and matched-label probes stay separate. No actual ADK runtime execution has been claimed.

title:
Feedback first.
Weight updates only with evidence.
lead: Evals, fine-tuning, preference learning and RL are different tools.
notes: ADK is an agent and evaluation framework, not a universal RL trainer. RLHF, preference optimization and RL require different data and optimization infrastructure; many APIs do not expose weight updates. Do not train on the holdout or let a system certify its own generated labels. The delivered bridge performs no model update.

title:
A calibrated instrument.
Not three years of proof.
lead: What works today—and the next evidence to collect.
notes: Present the validation record plainly. No model-provider efficacy measurements were made. The next study should integrate an actual scaffold, run independently authored held-out tasks and evaluate realistic monitors against adaptive attacks.

title:
Increase autonomy
as evidence improves.
lead: Test the system. Vary the conditions. Measure the consequences.
notes: Close with the practical call to action. The code and protocol are packaged locally; repository publishing is deferred. Leave time for questions. The aim is to replace a general claim of being ethical with specific, inspectable evidence about a defined workflow.

title: Research to read next
lead: Primary repository evidence reviewed; full-paper verification remains outstanding.
